question.problem:
Consider the rectangle $C$ with vertices $(-1,-1),(1,-1),(1,2),$ and $(-1,2),$ traversed counterclockwise. Using the flux form of Green's theorem, express the flux of the vector field
$F(x,y)=(6xy+y{x}^{2})\,i-{y}^{2}\,j$
through $C$ as a repeated integral.
question.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $F=P\,i+Q\,j,$ and $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first derivatives on an open region containing $D,$ then the flux form of Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∬}_{D}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}A,
$$

which is equivalent to

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14235132/assets/861b873005c03ea6c25255f2febc975ff153d939780ec46e4f4503cbb50640dc.png)

We have that $P(x,y)=6xy+y{x}^{2}$ and $Q(x,y)=-{y}^{2}.$ So,  

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=6y+2xy,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =-2y.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D=\{(x,y):-1\le x\le 1,\,-1\le y\le 2\}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem in flux form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(6y+2xy)+(-2y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{2}2y(2+x)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
